title: closing an http/2 stream a second time throws an exception
body:
h/t to @vkostyukov for finding this issue.  I'm just the messenger!

### Expected behavior

Closing an http/2 stream a second time should not have a performance impact

- Netty's internal (server-side) logic closes the stream via [closeForcibly](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/911b2acc5086415d762a2050609827b13c521dfd/codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2MultiplexCodec.java#L898-L900) (note usage of a VoidPromise,
- which triggers pipelie.fireChannelInactive() via [Http2ChannelUnsafe.close](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/911b2acc5086415d762a2050609827b13c521dfd/codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2MultiplexCodec.java#L851)
- which fails the async queue in the channel transport,
- which calls channel.close again,
- which ends up in the same [Http2ChannelUnsafe.close](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/911b2acc5086415d762a2050609827b13c521dfd/codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2MultiplexCodec.java#L851) method,
- which tries to assign a listener to a void promise (and fails)

By making sure that we don't close the stream a second time, we were able to achieve a 20% perf improvement.

### Steps to reproduce

Close an http/2 stream from Http2MultiplexCodec on the server-side after it has already been closed (note, streams are closed after the stream is finished, ie after one request and response).

### Netty version
4.1.16.Final

### JVM version (e.g. `java -version`)
jdk7

### OS version (e.g. `uname -a`)
centos7
